findings.current: Unless someone had an exceptionally thick liver, no one would think of crossing the plateau alone.
findings.defect: “Thick liver” is an untranslated Korean idiom and is not intelligible natural English.
findings.rationale: 간덩이가 붓다 describes extreme audacity or recklessness, not a physical condition of the liver.
findings.replacement: Unless someone was exceptionally daring, they would never even consider crossing the plateau alone.
findings.source: 어지간히 간덩이가 붓지 않고서야 혈혈단신의 몸으로 고원을 가로지를 생각은 하지 못한다.

findings.defect: The draft invents a plural object and says Black Sand stopped the speaker and others, although he only stopped the Human Butcher’s subordinate.
findings.rationale: The source asks generally why Black Sand is reacting that way; it does not say that he stopped “us.”

findings.current: “Where does a little bastard like you get off talking so formally? Are you from the Lower District Sect?”
findings.defect: The draft mischaracterizes 하오체 as simply formal speech, obscures why the elder considers it disrespectful, and loses the 하오체/하오문 wordplay.
findings.rationale: The old man rebukes a younger man for addressing him with the insufficiently respectful 하오체, then jokes that its name makes him sound like a member of 하오문.
findings.replacement:
“Who told a little bastard like you that he could use *hao*-style speech with me? Are you from the Lower District Sect or something?”[^1]

[^1]: *Hao*-style speech is a semi-formal Korean speech level; its name sets up the pun on the Lower District Sect’s Korean name, *Haomun*.

findings.defect: “Goodness” sanitizes the coarse, emphatic regional register of 아따 and 우라지게.
findings.rationale: The source uses rough, colorful speech rather than a mild exclamation, which is part of the old man’s abrupt voice shift.
findings.replacement: “Well, damn, you’ve laid out one hell of a feast.

findings.current: The next moment, the Human Butcher’s eyes rolled back, and his body shot upward like lightning.
findings.defect: The draft physicalizes the rage idiom 눈이 뒤집히다 as his eyes literally rolling back.
findings.rationale: Here 눈이 뒤집히다 means that rage has overwhelmed his reason, not that his eyes perform a distinct physical action.
findings.replacement: The next moment, the Human Butcher, beside himself with rage, shot upward like lightning.
findings.source: 다음 순간, 눈이 뒤집힌 인도의 신형이 번개처럼 솟구쳤다.

findings.current: The resulting sword pressure scattered the dust cloud, revealing a ruin that had been reduced to half rubble.
findings.defect: “Reduced to half rubble” is both unnatural and materially different from the ruin being half pulverized into powder.
findings.rationale: 반쯤 가루가 된 describes roughly half of the wreckage having been reduced to powder.
findings.replacement: The resulting sword pressure scattered the dust cloud, revealing a half-pulverized ruin.
findings.source: 그러자 검압에 의해 먼지구름이 흩어지며 반쯤 가루가 된 폐허가 모습을 드러냈다.

findings.current: The Human Butcher’s eyes were still rolled back. He had nothing left to restrain him.
findings.defect: The draft again turns an idiom for being beyond reason into a literal eye position.
findings.rationale: 눈이 뒤집힌 describes his maddened state, while 거리낄 것이 없었다 means he no longer had any hesitation or compunction.
findings.replacement: The Human Butcher was already beyond reason and had no reservations left.
findings.source: 이미 눈이 뒤집힌 인도는 거리낄 것이 없었다.

findings.current: “Mount Tai Presses Down on the Crown.”
findings.defect: Quotation marks turn the narrative technique name into dialogue, inventing a spoken declaration by the Human Butcher.
findings.rationale: The source presents the move name as a narration fragment and does not indicate that anyone says it aloud.
findings.replacement: *Mount Tai Presses Down on the Crown.*

findings.current: “There’s no part of a chicken to waste. It tastes good, you can boil the bones down and eat them, and sometimes I even use them for Sword Energy.”
findings.defect: The draft says the boiled bones themselves are eaten, changing the culinary explanation.
findings.rationale: 뼈는 푹 고아 먹고 refers to simmering the bones thoroughly to make and consume broth, not eating the bones themselves.
findings.replacement: “There’s no part of a chicken that goes to waste. The meat is delicious, the bones make a fine broth when simmered down, and sometimes they’re even good for wielding Sword Energy.”
findings.source: “닭은 버릴 곳이 없지. 맛도 좋고, 뼈는 푹 고아 먹고. 가끔은 검기도 쓰고.”

summary: Several actionable fidelity and register issues, including an altered subject, a lost speech-level pun, physicalized rage idioms, invented dialogue, and an incorrect culinary explanation.
